ownerAcceptance.scope: Reviewed relevance labels accepted; original benchmark remains preserved.

basis: Manual assistant review of original public-safe synthesis records, not source-transcript verification or independent human evaluation.

scale.3: Directly useful guidance for the question
scale.2: Useful adjacent context requiring an additional inference
scale.1: Incidental word overlap or weak connection

last-company.title: Michele Ferrero's $40 Billion Privately Owned Chocolate Empire
last-company.reason: Lessons 5 and 8 describe patient ownership and intrinsically rewarding work, but offer limited guidance for choosing one's company. The care match also includes employee medical care.

last-company.title: DHH: How to Build a Profitable Company Without Losing Control
last-company.reason: Lessons 6, 7 and 11 connect enjoyable work, independence and sustainable hours; these support staying with a company more than selecting one.

last-company.title: Lessons From Backing The Best Founders In Fintech | Micky Malka
last-company.reason: Lessons 5 and 8 give concrete long-term selection criteria: observed mission consistency, authenticity and founder traits worth staying in business with for decades. Investor/partner perspective must be disclosed when applying this to a founder's own choice.

last-company.title: How to Dominate for Decades | Doug Leone, Sequoia Capital
last-company.reason: Lessons 2, 3 and 5 concern conviction, holding winners and preserving founder identity. They are adjacent evidence, not an exclusive or clearly superior answer to choosing personally meaningful work for a decade.

hiring.title: Building Defense Technologies to Protect Democracies | Torsten Reil, Helsing
hiring.reason: Lessons 7 and 8 describe an early recruitment pipeline, performance calibration and exceptional people with initiative. Direct operational hiring evidence.

hiring.title: Breakfast with Brad Jacobs + How To Make A Few Billion Dollars
hiring.reason: Lessons 4 and 5 specify candidate judgment, willingness to leave a vacancy, compensation, recruiting and incentives. Direct criteria and process for recruiting capable people.

hiring.title: Ken Griffin: Founder of Citadel and Citadel Securities
hiring.reason: Lessons 2 and 5 show recruiting scientists and acquiring research leadership around a capability; narrower than a general exceptional-hiring method.

hiring.title: Elon Musk and The Early Days of SpaceX
hiring.reason: Lessons 2 and 7 explicitly describe recruiting through meaningful responsibility and credible commitment, plus hiring commercial expertise early. Direct recruiting mechanisms, even though they differ from Tobi's candidate-selection criteria.

hiring.title: Tobi Lütke: 21 Years of Building Shopify
hiring.reason: Lesson 3 explicitly recommends unusual strengths, high agency and nonconformity. Still highly relevant despite full-corpus rank 32; its omission is a recall limitation, not evidence that the leading results are irrelevant.

focus.title: Rockefeller's Autobiography
focus.reason: Lesson 7 explicitly recommends narrowing to oil and concentrating resources on one priority. Direct response to focusing on one thing.

focus.title: Building Defense Technologies to Protect Democracies | Torsten Reil, Helsing
focus.reason: The score combines simple hardware, managerial review focus and regulatory excuses as distraction across unrelated lessons. It lacks a coherent method for the user's focus problem.

focus.title: How Elon Thinks
focus.reason: Lessons 2, 4 and 5 give deletion, one binding bottleneck and one organizational metric to prevent distraction by secondary objectives.

focus.title: How Steve Jobs Kept Things Simple
focus.reason: Lessons 1, 4 and 5 emphasize one version, one focus per quarter and narrowing scope. Remains directly relevant; it is not the only valid precedent.
